summary_en: This work establishes a large-scale benchmark for photoacoustic image-quality assessment using nearly one million images from five datasets. It evaluates conventional full-reference and no-reference metrics and trains learned predictors, finding that structure-aware metrics are substantially more reliable than PSNR-like measures for photoacoustic reconstruction assessment.

summary_en: The paper introduces a dual-modal framework that uses co-registered ultrasound information to estimate and compensate heterogeneous sound speed in photoacoustic computed tomography. This reduces depth-dependent aberration where photoacoustic-only image cues become unreliable because of optical attenuation.

summary_en: The proposed adaptive residual attention network denoises full-field photoacoustic surface-displacement maps while explicitly preserving the sharp wavefront structures needed for reconstruction. A single noisy map is reported to approach the quality of coherent averaging over many acquisitions, enabling substantially faster non-contact FF-PAT.
